mappings.note: New wavelength and frequency from a changed time period (LO-6 + LO-79), then part (b) names pitch as the SUBJECTIVE property of sound, which is LO-73's perception half.

Same shape as L147 - f from v/lambda then an audibility judgement (CG2) - but this one lands at 33 kHz, outside the range. The pair are deliberately mapped alike because the frame has one code for audibility either way.
Two cliffs, two echo times, solve for speed and then for separation. CG2 for echo, LO-79 for the two-step prediction.
Distance to a submarine from a 4 s round trip. Same SONAR family and codes.

Two firing positions give two equations that must be set up and solved simultaneously, which is C8.1's 'mathematical model ... to manipulate variables' rather than a single substitution. That is what lifts it above the other echo numericals.
Vibrations per minute from a 100 Hz frequency. The same item as P8 with different numbers, and mapped the same way.
Time for an echo from a 660 m cliff. Unknown is a time rather than a distance, but the relation and the gap are identical, so the codes are too.
Speed from f and lambda, then a travel time over 1.5 km. No reflection anywhere, so this stays with LO-6 rather than CG2.
The same two-stage fall-plus-sound structure as L142, and mapped the same way: LO-77 for decomposing the real event into its two contributing times, LO-6 and LO-79 for the sound leg.
Cliff distance from a 2 s echo at 346 m/s. Same family as L130, L137 and L158.
The slinky-with-a-ribbon case study: the coils are compressions and rarefactions and the ribbon shows particles oscillating in place (LO-5), demonstrated through an explicit physical model (C8.1).
Pitch and loudness (LO-73), timbre (only C2.7's text covers it), and the whole item is set in music across two instruments, which is C5.3's scope.
Three parts, three different outcomes: the taut string as a SOLID medium (LO-3), the loose string failing to vibrate (LO-2), and why it would not work in space (LO-4).
Crests and troughs read as compressions and rarefactions (LO-5), wavelength and the frequency/time-period relation (LO-6), and the perceived higher note (LO-73).
The echo case study: name the phenomenon, state the 0.1 s condition, then compute total distance and cliff distance. CG2 for the uncovered echo content, LO-79 for the two computations.
Why steel carries sound faster than air (LO-3), what happens to wavelength at fixed frequency (LO-6), set as a real-life observation whose cause must be identified (LO-77).
Concert-hall reverberation and absorbent materials. LO-75 for the built acoustic space; the item is recall of the standard remedy, so no LO-77 - that is what separates it from C169.
Thicker vocal cords vibrate more slowly (LO-1 for the vibrating part, LO-6 for the frequency), which is heard as a lower pitch, with loudness contrasted (LO-73).

Why an echo returns from a cliff but not inside a small room: the student must analyse two real situations and identify the distance factor that separates them (LO-77). CG2 for echo, which has no outcome.
Audible range, infrasound and ultrasound with animal examples: LO-6 for the frequency bands, CG2 for the hearing limits and the two categories that no outcome names.

Unlike C165 this one requires DIAGNOSING why the hall failed and judging why a curved ceiling helps, so LO-77 joins LO-75 and CG2. The diagnosis is the real difference between the two hall case studies.
Names ultrasound and pins it to a frequency above 20 kHz (LO-6), and explains inaudibility against the human range (CG2). Mapped on the frequency classification, not on the medical use.

Ultrasonography: how the image is formed from reflections and why ordinary sound will not do. LO-77 for analysing the mechanism, CG2 for ultrasound. Distinguished from C170, which only classifies the wave by frequency.

SONAR named (CG2), then part (b) asks why the pulse travels faster in seawater than in air - a comparison across states of matter, which is LO-3. That second part is what separates it from the other SONAR case studies.
The eardrum and the definition of intensity have no outcome anywhere in the frame, so CG2; LO-73 covers only the loudness/amplitude part. Recorded as a poor fit - this is the ear-anatomy gap again.
